title.text: Every stage of the lifecycle, with a skill behind it

lead.text: Lead with the plain-English verb, then the code name. Each card names the skills that run the stage and whether it is available today.

intake.title: Intake and spec
intake.text: A raw idea interviewed into a decision-complete brief, challenged, then filed as one issue.

build.title: Build
build.text: One request per turn in an isolated worktree: warm up, author, verify, commit locally. Never pushes.

review.title: Review and test
review.text: Adversarial review before the PR, the impacted suites, coverage against the ladder.

pr.title: PR to Ready
pr.text: Push when you decide, one PR with a composed body, then the readiness watch to your merge prompt.

backlog.title: Backlog operations
backlog.text: A severity band, a label, a hand-picked list or the whole surface-matched backlog, delivered to gates.

release.title: Release
release.text: The tag cut with its own proposal PR, a non-production send, and publication only on your typed go.

adopt.title: Adopt and maintain
adopt.text: Make a repository a consumer, keep its canon mirror current, raise runners, install a CI tier, update Hatsu.

validate.title: Validate and clean up
validate.text: Post-merge UI validation on your call, the leftovers inventoried and removed only as you picked.

title.text: The layers, and the five human gates

lead.text: Nen at the base, Hatsu on top, the Handbooks as canon. The Cloud tier is the future autonomous plane; the Library is roadmap. Select a layer or a gate.

gatesLead.text: Agents propose; you decide. Hatsu drives work to a gate and stops there.

lead.text: One checkout serves every surface. Pick yours: the install command, the session command, a first request, and the Nen bootstrap at the version Hatsu pins.

hidden.text: This page is hidden from production builds behind SHOW_PRICING.

free.a: Yes. Nen, Hatsu and the Handbooks are MIT licensed, fully open source, public and free. A hosted tier is coming later and is not for sale yet.

agents.a: Hatsu runs inside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Antigravity. A tier is named, never a model version: frontier for your own session, deep for reviewers, fast for workers, economy for watchers. The live model id is read from your surface when a skill runs.
agents.source: Brand pillars § 4; hatsu README § Models and surfaces

merge.q: Does it merge or publish on its own?
merge.a: No. Every PR ends at your merge prompt, and publication runs only on your typed go. Agents propose; you decide at the gates.

where.a: On your machine, in the agent you already use, on your own credentials. There is no hosted Bankai today.

pays.a: You do, with your own key or subscription on the surface you run. The future Cloud tier will also require your own model API key.

stacks.a: The Handbooks cover SwiftUI+TCA, Jetpack Compose and React+Redux Toolkit, plus baselines for security, UX, release and quality that apply everywhere.

update.a: Run the update skill on your surface: it fast-forwards the checkout you keep and ends with the one thing left to type.

hosted.a: Not yet. Hosted, autonomous runs are coming later, unnamed and unpriced until then.
